claims.text: Introducing coherent precipitates into FeCoNi-based fcc high-entropy alloys will increase coercive field.
Coherent precipitates act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning reduces magnetic domain size.
Domain-wall pinning increases the energy required for domain-wall motion.
The increased energy required for domain-wall motion will increase coercivity.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have a coercive field greater than 100 Oe.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have greater coercivity than single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a derivative without coherent precipitates.
The hypothesis is bounded to FeCoNi-based alloys having an fcc matrix and potential secondary phases.
The precipitate size and distribution needed for optimal coercivity enhancement depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome uses greater than 100 Oe as an absolute final coercive-field threshold, whereas the falsification rule can be read as requiring an increase greater than 100 Oe relative to the control. These are different criteria.
